_comment: Microsoft Edge manifest. Edge is Chromium, so functionally this is the
Chrome manifest and the interesting decision is what was NOT changed.
THE "key" FIELD IS KEPT ON PURPOSE. The instinct is to strip it, because
the Edge Add-ons store assigns its own ID and ignores it. But Atlas does
not deliver this extension through a store -- electron/ipc/extension.js
copies the folder to disk and the user side-loads it unpacked. For an
unpacked Chromium extension the ID is derived from "key" when present and
from the install PATH when absent. Keeping the key means an Edge side-load
gets the SAME extension ID as Chrome, and therefore the same
chrome-extension:// origin, and therefore already passes the CORS allowlist
in electron/rpc/extensionServer.js with no server change at all.
Strip the key and every user gets a different path-derived ID, no allowlist
entry can exist, and Edge silently fails CORS on every RPC call while
looking perfectly installed.
IF THIS IS EVER PUBLISHED TO THE EDGE ADD-ONS STORE, that changes: Partner
Center assigns a fixed ID, the key is ignored, and the resulting
chrome-extension://<edge-id> origin must be added to EDGE_STORE_EXTENSION_ID
in electron/rpc/extensionServer.js. That constant exists and is empty for
exactly this reason.
This file is kept as a real file rather than derived from manifest.json by
the packaging script so that the reasoning above lives next to the artifact
it explains. scripts/check-extension-manifests.js asserts it stays in sync
with the Chrome manifest on every field that is not deliberately different.
